overview: Denmark is a country in northern Europe, made up of the Jutland peninsula and hundreds of islands. Its capital, Copenhagen, is on the island of Zealand. Denmark is one of the oldest monarchies in the world, and the self-governing territories of Greenland and the Faroe Islands are also part of the Danish realm. It joined what is now the European Union in 1973 but kept its own currency, the krone.

geography.text: Denmark is very low and flat: no point in the country is much more than 170 metres above sea level. Jutland, which joins Germany in the south, makes up most of the land, and the rest is islands such as Zealand, Funen and Bornholm. With the North Sea to the west and the Baltic to the east, nowhere in Denmark is far from the coast.

history.text: Danish Vikings raided and settled across north-western Europe, and at times Danish kings ruled England, Norway and Sweden. Norway stayed under Danish rule until 1814. Denmark adopted a democratic constitution in 1849, was occupied by Germany during the Second World War, and joined what is now the European Union in 1973.

events.title: Cnut rules England
events.text: The Danish king Cnut becomes king of England.

events.title: Kalmar Union
events.text: Denmark, Norway and Sweden are united under one monarch.

events.title: German occupation
events.text: Germany occupies Denmark for the rest of the Second World War.

events.title: Joins the EEC
events.text: Denmark joins the European Economic Community.

government.text: Denmark is a constitutional monarchy, with a king as head of state and a Prime Minister leading the government. The Folketing, its parliament, has one chamber. Greenland and the Faroe Islands are self-governing parts of the Danish realm. Denmark joined NATO as a founding member and what is now the European Union in 1973, but it uses its own currency, the krone.

economy.text: Denmark is one of the richest countries in the world and has a large welfare state paid for by high taxes. It is a world leader in wind power: turbines produce around half of its electricity. Medicines, shipping, food and design are major industries.

culture.text: Danes are known for hygge, a feeling of cosiness and comfort. Hans Christian Andersen, author of The Little Mermaid and The Ugly Duckling, was Danish. So is LEGO, the toy brick invented in Billund, whose name comes from the Danish words for 'play well'.

items.title: LEGO
items.text: Founded in Billund in 1932; the plastic brick as we know it dates from 1958.

items.title: Hans Christian Andersen
items.text: Wrote more than 150 fairy tales, translated into over 100 languages.

items.title: The Little Mermaid
items.text: A bronze statue in Copenhagen's harbour since 1913.

sport.text: Football is the most popular sport in Denmark, and the national team won the European Championship in 1992 after being called up at the last minute. Denmark is also one of the world's best handball nations, and cycling is huge both as sport and as everyday transport.

items.title: Euro 1992
items.text: Denmark replaced Yugoslavia ten days before the tournament and won it.

items.title: Handball
items.text: The men's team won Olympic gold in 2016 and 2024.

items.title: Tour de France 2022
items.text: Started in Copenhagen; a Dane, Jonas Vingegaard, won it.
